# Lecture Delivery

## Opening (2 minutes)

> "Today we're adding two critical layers to our reproducibility toolkit:
> renv for package management and Docker for environment containerization.
> By the end of class, you'll have an ADNI analysis environment that any
> collaborator can reproduce exactly on any machine."

**Set expectations:**

- This is more complex than Lecture 6
- Docker build takes time - we'll use waiting productively
- TA will help with Docker issues

## Part I: Concepts Review (10 minutes)

### The Reproducibility Problem

Start with a story:

> "Imagine you've completed your ADNI analysis. Six months later, a
> reviewer asks for a revision. You run your code and get different
> results - or worse, errors. Package updates have broken your analysis."

### Two-Layer Solution

Draw on whiteboard or show slide:

```
Your Code
   ↓
R Packages (renv locks versions)
   ↓
R + System Libraries (Docker locks everything)
   ↓
Operating System (Docker base image)
```

**Key point:** renv alone isn't enough because:

- R version can change
- System libraries can change
- OS updates can break things

### Quick Conceptual Questions

Ask students:

- "What does renv::snapshot() do?"
- "What's the difference between a Docker image and container?"

## Part V: Initialize renv (15 minutes)

### Step 10: renv::init()

**Demo first**, explain what's created:

```r
renv::init()
```

Show the new files:

- `renv/` folder - project-specific library
- `renv.lock` - the lockfile (JSON format)
- `.Rprofile` - auto-activates renv

**Open renv.lock and explain the structure:**

```r
file.edit("renv.lock")
```

> "This JSON file records the exact version of every package. When someone
> runs renv::restore(), they get these exact versions."

### Step 11: Install Packages

**Install one at a time, explain each:**

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")   # Data manipulation
install.packages("survival")    # Survival analysis for ADNI
install.packages("tableone")    # Baseline characteristics
install.packages("ggfortify")   # Survival plots
```

**This takes time** - use it to:

- Answer questions
- Preview Docker concepts
- Discuss ADNI analysis approaches

### Step 12: Snapshot

```r
renv::snapshot()
```

**Show the updated renv.lock:**

> "Notice how it now includes all 150+ packages including dependencies"


## Part VI: Create Dockerfile (10 minutes)

### Steps 13-15: Dockerfile Creation

**Explain each line as you type:**

```dockerfile
# Start from Rocker's R image with specific version
FROM rocker/r-ver:4.4.0

# Install system libraries needed by R packages
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev \  # For httr, curl packages
    libssl-dev \            # For openssl package
    libxml2-dev \           # For xml2 package
    ...

# Set working directory inside container
WORKDIR /workspace

# Install renv
RUN R -e "install.packages('renv', repos='https://cloud.r-project.org')"

# Copy renv files (not the actual packages!)
COPY renv.lock renv.lock
COPY renv/activate.R renv/activate.R

# Restore packages from lockfile
RUN R -e "renv::restore()"

# Default command when container starts
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

### Step 16: .dockerignore

**Explain why we exclude files:**

> "We don't want to include raw data in the image - it should stay local.
> We also exclude .git to keep the image small."


## Part VII: Build and Test (15 minutes)

### Step 17: Build Image

**This is the longest step.** Start the build:

```bash
docker build -t yourusername/adni-analysis:v1 .
```

**While it builds:**

- Explain what's happening at each step
- Answer questions about Dockerfiles
- Discuss how this enables collaboration

### Step 18-19: Test Container

**Once built, run interactively:**

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$(pwd):/workspace" yourusername/adni-analysis:v1
```

**Explain the flags:**

- `--rm` - Remove container when done
- `-it` - Interactive terminal
- `-v "$(pwd):/workspace"` - Mount local files

**Inside container:**

```r
R
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
sessionInfo()
```

**Show that versions match renv.lock**


## Part VIII: Version Control (5 minutes)

### Steps 20-22: Git, GitHub, DockerHub

Move quickly - similar to Lecture 6.

**Key addition:**

```bash
docker push yourusername/adni-analysis:v1
```

> "Now anyone can pull your exact environment from DockerHub"


## Part IX: Verification (5 minutes)

### Steps 23-24: Final Checks

**Simulate collaborator workflow:**

```bash
# In a different directory
git clone https://github.com/username/adni.yourname.git
cd adni.yourname
docker pull username/adni-analysis:v1
docker run --rm -it -v "$(pwd):/workspace" username/adni-analysis:v1
```

> "This is exactly what a collaborator would do. They get your code from
> GitHub and your environment from DockerHub."


## Closing (3 minutes)

**Recap the reproducibility stack:**

> "You now have three layers of reproducibility:
> 1. Your code is on GitHub
> 2. Your package versions are locked in renv.lock
> 3. Your entire environment is containerized in Docker
>
> A collaborator can reproduce your exact analysis environment with
> three commands: git clone, docker pull, docker run."

**Assign homework:**

> "Before February 17, fill in your ADNI analysis plan. If you add new
> packages, run renv::snapshot() and rebuild your Docker image."


# Troubleshooting Guide

## Docker Issues

### "Cannot connect to Docker daemon"

Docker Desktop not running. Start the application.

### "docker build fails at apt-get"

Network issue. Try:

```bash
docker build --network=host -t myimage .
```

### "Permission denied"

On Linux:

```bash
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
# Then log out and back in
```

Or use sudo:

```bash
sudo docker build -t myimage .
```

### "No space left on device"

Clean up old images:

```bash
docker system prune -a
```

### Build is very slow

Pre-pull the base image:

```bash
docker pull rocker/r-ver:4.4.0
```

## renv Issues

### "renv::restore() fails in Docker"

Check that files are not in `.dockerignore`:

- `renv.lock`
- `renv/activate.R`
- `.Rprofile`

### "Package not available"

Add repository to renv:

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
renv::restore()
```

### "Binary not available"

Package needs compilation. Add system dependencies to Dockerfile.


## Common Package System Dependencies

| R Package | System Library |
|-----------|----------------|
| curl, httr | libcurl4-openssl-dev |
| openssl | libssl-dev |
| xml2 | libxml2-dev |
| systemfonts | libfontconfig1-dev |
| textshaping | libharfbuzz-dev, libfribidi-dev |
| ragg | libfreetype6-dev, libpng-dev |
| haven | (none - pure R) |
| readxl | (none - pure R) |

## Common Post-Class Questions

**"My Docker build takes forever"**

- Pre-pull base image
- Use Docker layer caching (don't change early Dockerfile lines)
- Consider using a pre-built image with common packages

**"Can I use a different base image?"**

- Yes, rocker/tidyverse includes tidyverse pre-installed
- But locks you to their package versions

**"How do I add a new package after building?"**

1. Install in R: `install.packages("newpkg")`
2. Update lockfile: `renv::snapshot()`
3. Rebuild image: `docker build -t user/image:v2 .`
4. Push: `docker push user/image:v2`

**"Is Docker required for the course?"**

- Encouraged but not strictly required
- renv alone provides good reproducibility
- Docker adds OS-level reproducibility
